Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the time this week. A couple of follow-ups from KiteLogistics' engineering team around how our billing units behave for longer conversation windows and bursty jobs. Short version: they need deterministic examples we can map back to their invoice and procurement team. Can you confirm the scenarios below (and I can follow up with a worked example once we agree on the rules):

1) Long-context chat (single session, 40k tokens across 10 requests). Does Redwood bill per-request token totals and then apply rounding/minimums per request, or do we aggregate across the session and apply a single rounding at the session level?
2) Streaming responses: are token measurements done per-stream-chunk (e.g., every 1k tokens or per 60s window) or by the whole response once the stream ends?
3) Embeddings/aux calls: do embeddings generated in the same flow count toward the same meter as generation tokens or are they a separate line item?
4) Minimums & rounding: what is the per-request minimum (if any), and what quantum do we round to (e.g., nearest 100 tokens)?

Separately: KiteLogistics is asking whether their committed discount band should apply to burst traffic (spike above committed baseline) or only to baseline volume. If you can confirm current policy and whether we can offer a one-off concession for the pilot, that would help close the PO.

I'll attach the sample usage CSV they sent so you can see the pattern.

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the clear list. A few clarifications from our side before you prepare examples:

- For long-context chat, our internal legal wants a simple mapping on the invoice (they dislike many small line items). If you aggregate at session level we can map per-session lines; if per-request, we need a predictable upper bound.
- Streaming: we prefer per-response billing if that simplifies mapping, but we need to be sure that partial/failing streams don't leave us underbilled or overbilled.
- Embeddings: these are used for similarity lookups and are separate budget lines for us — if they get mixed with generation tokens it complicates forecasting.
- Discount: our procurement team wants committed discount to apply to baseline only; they expect overage billed at a higher rate, but they asked whether Redwood can cap overage for the first two months of the pilot.

Can you (1) send an example invoice that shows both per-request and per-session mappings for their usage sample, and (2) confirm whether we can get a capped overage for April/May as a pilot concession?

Priyom / Sergio —

Looping you both for a quick policy + ops confirmation and a recommended customer-facing mapping. KiteLogistics (large pilot) wants:
- A single mapping for their invoice team (prefer aggregated session lines if possible)
- A cap on overage for the first two months (procurement request)

Summary of what I think we should offer (please confirm edits):

Proposal A (session-aggregate billing, recommended):
- Metering key: session_id (customer-provided session id or generated by Redwood).
- Billing unit: sum of request + response tokens within session window.
- Rounding: round up to nearest 100 tokens per session.
- Minimum: sessions with less than 64 tokens billed as 64 tokens (per-session minimum) to avoid microline noise.
- Streaming: stream chunks counted immediately; final session total used for rounding (so partial streams still accumulate to session total).
- Embeddings: billed as separate line item (embeddings tokens measured independently) — we do not mix with generation tokens.
- Discount: committed discount applies to baseline only; overage billed at list, but offer a one-time capped overage (max 20% of baseline spend) for April+May as a pilot concession.

Rationale: Session aggregation gives Kite a small number of invoice lines and predictable rounding; rounding at session-level reduces per-request noise for long conversations. The 64-token minimum avoids many micro-lines and is consistent with our small-request thresholds.

Operational notes (for Sergio):
- Need to confirm how we identify session_id when customer doesn't pass one (use connection id + user id heuristics).
- Need a one-off billing rule for cap: track overage and emit credit if over the cap.

If that looks okay I can send an example invoice mapping and the SLA addendum for signature.

Thanks —

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the patience. Priyom and Sergio confirmed the recommended mapping below. I've attached a worked example invoice (sample_invoice_mapping.xlsx) that takes the CSV you sent and shows two views (per-request lines vs session-aggregate lines) plus the proposed SLA addendum PDF that captures the one-time cap for April/May. Summary of final rules: 

- Metering: prefer session-level when customer supplies session_id. If none supplied, Redwood will group by ephemeral conversation id for up to 24 hours of inactivity.
- Token accounting: all request and generation tokens within the session count toward the session total. Embeddings are billed as separate line items and will remain on a separate invoice row.
- Rounding: session totals (sum of tokens across session) rounded up to nearest 100 tokens.
- Minimum: per-session minimum of 64 tokens. (Matches internal small-request threshold.)
- Streaming: counted immediately toward session total; if a stream fails mid-response the tokens billed are the tokens seen by the runtime — they still contribute to the session total and will be rounded at the end of the session window.
- Discount & cap: committed discount will apply to baseline only; overage billed at list. For the pilot we will apply a capped overage credit: if overage charges for Apr+May exceed 20% of baseline spend, Redwood will apply a credit to limit customer bills to baseline + 20% for those months. Credit will appear as an invoice adjustment.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached sample invoice mapping (sheet: Session-Aggregate) and confirm that format works for Kite's FP&A.
2) If acceptable, sign the SLA addendum (DocuSign link included in the PDF). Once signed, we'll enable session-aggregation meters for your account and turn on the pilot cap.

Attachments: sample_invoice_mapping.xlsx (XLSX, 58 KB), proposed_sla_addendum.pdf (PDF, 46 KB)
